messages.text: Visualize how quicksort partitions an array with an animation

Quicksort is a highly efficient, "divide and conquer" sorting algorithm. At its heart lies the **partition** process—a clever way of organizing elements so that the algorithm can solve smaller sub-problems independently. ### What is Partitioning?

Partitioning is the procedure of rearranging an array (or a portion of it) around a specific element called the pivot. After a partition, the pivot is in its final sorted position, with all smaller elements to its left and all larger elements to its right.

Think of partitioning like a librarian organizing a shelf of books by height. They pick one book as a reference (the pivot). Every book shorter than the reference goes to the left side, and every book taller goes to the right. Even if the left and right groups aren't perfectly sorted yet, the reference book itself is exactly where it needs to be. ### How the Partition Mechanism Works To understand the movement, we usually look at the **Lomuto Partition Scheme**, which is one of the most common ways to implement this logic. Here is how it flows: 1. **Select a Pivot:** Usually, the last element in the array is chosen as the pivot. 2. **The Pointer Chase:** We use two pointers. One pointer ($j$) scans through the array looking for elements smaller than the pivot. The other pointer ($i$) marks the "boundary" of the smaller-element zone. 3. **Swapping:** Whenever $j$ finds an element smaller than the pivot, we expand the "small zone" by incrementing $i$ and swapping the elements at $i$ and $j$. 4. **The Final Swap:** Once $j$ reaches the end, the pivot is swapped into the position right after the "small zone."
  • The Pivot's Finality: Once a partition is complete, the pivot element never moves again. It is officially "sorted."
  • Divide and Conquer: The algorithm then repeats this same process on the left and right sub-arrays until the entire list is organized.
  • In-place: One of Quicksort's biggest advantages is that it sorts the array without needing extra memory for new lists.
